newsitem.title: USA: Iraqi to stand trial July 16 for trade center bomb.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi to stand trial July 16 for trade center bomb.

text.p: The accused mastermind of the devastating 1993 World Trade Centre bombing will go on trial on July 16 for his alleged role in the blast that killed six people and injured thousands, a judge said on Friday.
Ramzi Ahmed Yousef, a Moslem militant who holds an Iraqi passport, was indicted in 1993 on charges of taking part in the bombing along with four others who were convicted in 1994.

Yousef was one of the world's most wanted fugitives with a $2 million bounty on his head for the attack until he was captured in Islamabad, Pakistan in February, 1995. Prosecutors said he had left the United States on the day of the bombing.
His co-defendant, Eyad Ismoil, a Jordanian, is accused of driving the van that carried the 1,200-pound fertiliser bomb into the basement garage of the World Trade Centre complex.
Yousef and two accomplices were convicted last year of conspiring to bomb 12 U.S. commercial airliners over the Pacific Ocean to punish the United States for backing Israel.
Unlike his first trial when he defended himself, Yousef, who has no formal legal training, has decided this time to rely on his court-appointed lawyer, Roy Kulcsar.

U.S. District Judge Kevin Duffy on Friday set a June 16 hearing on the reliability of the FBI's scientific laboratory. Scientist-agent Frederic Whitehurst and others allege that parts of the FBI lab are contaminated and that supervisors slanted reports and testimony to favour the prosecution.

Testifying at the trial of Sheikh Omar Abdel-Rahman in August 1995, Whitehurst, who was suspended from the FBI, said he disagreed with the final FBI report used by the government at the trade centre trial.

"There was a great deal of pressure put upon me to bias my interpretation," he said, adding that his superiors told him "not to provide alternative theories that could be used by the defence. I was told not to give the defence anything that could be used."

He also testified that initial reports about the presence of urea nitrate were false and that he was so upset about false testimony being used that he formulated urea nitrate from his own urine and placed that sample with others taken from the bomb scene to prove his point. He said the FBI technician failed to notice the difference.
Urea and nitrate are two of the chemical ingredients prosecutors said was used in the bomb.
